articles.title: A Blow to Voting Rights: Supreme Court Lets Stand Ruling That Bars Private Lawsuits in 7 States
articles.summary: Need help voting because of a disability or language barrier? The Supreme Court just allowed a ruling that strips private groups of the right to sue under a key Voting Rights Act protection in seven Midwestern states. Critics say this could gut enforcement.

articles.title: Alan Greenspan, Legendary Fed Chair Who Shaped the U.S. Economy, Dies at 100
articles.summary: He was the most famous central banker in the world—a jazz-loving economist whose words could move markets. Alan Greenspan, who led the Federal Reserve for nearly two decades, died Monday at 100. His legacy includes historic booms and a devastating crash.

articles.title: Keir Starmer Resigns as UK Prime Minister After Party Revolt
articles.summary: Besieged by dire polls, cabinet resignations, and a surging rival, UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer quit Monday. His departure sets the stage for Andy Burnham to potentially enter 10 Downing Street within weeks—an unprecedented political whirlwind.
